'''''Zephyranthes candida''''', with [[common name]]s that include '''autumn zephyrlily''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=ZECA|taxon=Zephyranthes candida|access-date=9 August 2015}}</ref> '''white windflower''',<ref name=APNI/> '''white rain lily''',<ref name = GRIN>{{GRIN}}</ref> and '''Peruvian swamp lily''',<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/19213/Zephyranthes-candida/Details |title=Royal Horticultural Society: Find a Plant |access-date=20 December 2014}}</ref> is a [[species]] of [[Zephyranthes|rain lily]] native to [[South America]] including [[Argentina]], [[Uruguay]], [[Paraguay]], and [[Brazil]]. The species is widely cultivated as an ornamental and reportedly naturalized in many places ([[South Africa]], the [[Indian subcontinent]], [[Zimbabwe]], [[Seychelles]], central and southern [[China]], [[Korea]], [[Nansei-shoto]] ([[Ryukyu Islands]]), [[Bhutan]], [[Solomon Islands]], [[Queensland]], [[Nauru]], [[Tonga]], [[Society Islands]], [[Mariana Islands]], southeastern [[United States]] (from [[Texas]] to [[North Carolina]]), the [[Lesser Antilles]], and [[Peru]]).<ref>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=291809 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref><ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Zephyranthes%20candida.png Biota of North American Program]</ref>

==Description==
[[File:Zephyranthes candida Herb. capsule fruit.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Zephyranthes candida Herb. capsule fruit]]
[[File:Zephyranthes candida 2024.jpg|thumb|right|''Zephyranthes candida'' flowering]]
Leaves are a deep glossy green and measure 3 [[Millimetre|mm]] wide. Flowers, which bud late in August (when propagated in the [[Northern Hemisphere]]) at first resemble a new leaf, but emerge from their papery sheaves to a stunning whiteness; they are erect in perianth white and sometimes pinkish abaxially. The leaf-like [[bract]] is 1.8 to 4 cm. They grow best in full sun to part shade and require a medium wet soil. Propagation is done by dividing [[bulb]]s or offsets and from seed.<ref name="jennifertitley">[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/488850#page/2/mode/1up Herbert, William. 1826. Botanical Magazine 53: pl. 2607, ''Zephyranthes candida'' ]</ref><ref name="poppystrode">[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/131753#page/107/mode/1up Lindley, John. 1823. Botanical Register  9: pl. 724, ''Amaryllis candida'' ]</ref><ref>Sasaki, Shun-ichi. 1928. List of Plants of Formosa 112, as ''Atamosco candida''</ref><ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/7430504#page/356/mode/1up Rafinesque, Constantine Samuel. 1838.  Flora Telluriana 4: 10. as ''Plectronema candida'' ]</ref>

==Taxonomy==
''Zephyranthes candida'' was first described by [[John Lindley]] in 1823 as ''Amaryllis candida''.<ref name="poppystrode"/> It was transferred to its current [[genus]] in 1826 by [[William Herbert (botanist)|William Herbert]].<ref name="jennifertitley"/><ref name=APNI>{{APNI|id=44569|name=''Zephyranthes candida''}}</ref> Other common names of ''Zephyranthes candida'' include August rain lily, white zephyr lily, white fairy lily, white rain lily, and autumn zephyr lily.{{citation needed|date=December 2014}}

== Cultivation ==
Hardiness: [[Hardiness zone#USDA hardiness zones|USDA zones]] 7-10.{{citation needed|date=April 2012}}
